meta.decision: Phase 199: tests/golden/wire_dict_baseline.json is preserved byte-unchanged. This file is the committed, reviewable expected-delta list the single datasheet-cited Fujitsu VPP correction in tools/datasheet_overrides.json produces on top of it -- on the same terms as the 197 and 198 layers, the golden itself is never re-captured or re-baselined to make this phase's change disappear.
meta.honesty: This layer records only that this one record's vpp_mv wire value moved from the pre-199 decoded 18000 to 21000. It does not by itself establish that 21000 is electrically correct -- the figure was read from a vendored datasheet page, not measured on a bench. It also makes no claim that the shield can deliver 21 V to socket pin 1; that question belongs to Phase 199's bench-measurement plan, not to this fixture.
meta.how_to_update: This layer is regenerated by the same script against the live database and never edited by hand. A new delta must name the chips and the reason in the commit message. Growing this list without a provenance justification is exactly the re-baselining the decision above exists to prevent -- see tests/test_wire_dict_equivalence.py's composition test for the anti-laundering assertions this fixture must satisfy.
meta.provenance: The record is attributable to the FUJITSU/MBM27128 entry in tools/datasheet_overrides.json (electrical.vpp_mv 18000 -> 21000, citing datasheets/MBM27128.pdf). Generated programmatically from the live capture against the committed golden plus the 149, 153, 182, 194, 197 and 198 delta layers -- never transcribed by hand, since the |<i> record-key suffix is a positional index within each manufacturer's list and would silently rot if any row is ever added or reordered.
